Every clause of Proposition 7.6 is stated in Lean, in full generality (arbitrary real exponent, arbitrary unrestricted real two-vector request), by theorems I read in source: the definition (7.31) is SignedCovariance.increment plus SignedWaveUpdate.signedVector; the W_{α−1/2} bound is signedVector_class; the derivative bound (7.33) is signed_quotient_class; the cross identity (7.34)/(7.32) is cross_reconstruct lifted to physical_signed_cross_covariance, whose symmetric double average is exactly the paper's B; the M_{2α−1} class is native_signed_square_class; the smooth zero extension at the shell edges, jointly in all slow parameters and with the √ζ edge weight, is extendedIncrement_regular. The only differences I found are packaging (three theorems, not one), the ε-normalization of the request, and the unstated — but definitionally immediate — linearity in Σ. None is a mathematical weakening, so the verdict is OK with relation different_formulation.

findings.summary: No single declaration states (7.32). Its three clauses are three separate general theorems in two modules; conjoining them is routine but is nowhere written as one statement of Proposition 7.6.
The Lean theorems take the already-ε-divided request R = Σ/ε as the input, not Σ. Hence exponents read β + 1/2 and 2β rather than α − 1/2 and 2α − 1.
The paper's words '(7.31) defines a linear operation LΣ' have no corresponding declaration: no lemma states Σ ↦ LΣ is additive or homogeneous.
